\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਦਲੀਲ} (dalīl)}{ਦਲੀਲ (dalīl)}]{\pa{ਦਲੀਲ} (dalīl) — an argument; a reason given in support}

\label{lesson:PA-C344-dalil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a matter, then the Punjabi for proof.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਦਲੀਲ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਦਲੀਲ}} — \emph{dalīl} — \textquotedblleft{}an argument; a reason given in support\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਤੁਹਾਡੀ} \pa{ਦਲੀਲ} \pa{ਠੀਕ} \pa{ਨਹੀਂ} \pa{ਹੈ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tuhāḍī dalīl ṭhīk nahīṁ hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your argument is not right.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਦਲੀਲ}} (\emph{dalīl}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{dalīl}, \textquotedblleft{}guide\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dalīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dalīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuhāḍī dalīl ṭhīk nahīṁ hai.} — Your argument is not right.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for a matter, then the Punjabi for proof, then say \emph{dalīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
